I farm the way I have done for years. I start from what worked last year, then I change a little if prices or weather push me. On 9 mu, I cannot gamble. Wheat and maize are my main food-and-cash fields, and with well water I will keep those steady. Cotton takes more watching and more spray, but if I keep a few mu, it still gives me some cash, so I will not drop it all at once. Around here, if a variety did well on other people’s land and stood up okay, I will use that kind. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard. If I save 20 or 30 yuan on fertilizer and lose yield, that hurts more than using a bit extra. For wheat I will feed it a bit heavier because wheat shows quickly if it is short of fertilizer. For maize I will follow after wheat and keep the field simple so I can manage the busy season. Cotton I will keep on a smaller piece because it needs more labor and more spraying, and my family has people working outside.

I will split the 9 mu like this: 6 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, then 3 mu in cotton. Wheat and maize are safer for me because I know the work, the well can support them, and the yield is steadier. I will use improved seed for wheat, hybrid seed for maize, and an improved cotton seed that people around me have already planted with decent results. I will plough the cotton ground well, and for wheat and maize I will use rotary tillage to save labor and time. I will water wheat about 3 times if the year is normal, maize 2 times, and cotton 3 times. Spray count I will keep practical: wheat 2 times, maize 2 times, cotton more often, about 4 times, because insects on cotton can turn bad fast.
